title: The Great Tours: England, Scotland and Wales
description:
S01 E03 — Roman Britain
The Roman conquest; how the Romans invaded Great Britain and spread their territory; Hadrian's Wall marking the edge of the empire; the Roman impact on Great Britain, from the city of Bath to the island's long and straight roads.

title: The Great Tours: England, Scotland and Wales
description:
S01 E04 — Anglo-Saxon and Viking Britain
How a number of Germanic tribes stepped in to fill the power vacuum left after the Romans left Britain; exploring the Anglo-Saxon conquests; the Viking attacks in the Middle Ages; Offa's Dyke and the monastery of Lindisfarne.

title: Crimes of the Century: A Selective History of Infamy
description:
S01 E01 — A Murder That Almost Killed Hollywood
Unsolved murders are as compelling as anything one might see in movies; the first "crime of the century" is the mysterious murder of a Hollywood director in 1922; William Desmond Taylor is not who he seems to be, and his death continues to fascinate.

title: Crimes of the Century: A Selective History of Infamy
description:
S01 E02 — The Deadly Irish Fairy Tale of 1895
The murder of Bridget Cleary in turn-of-the-century Ireland shows the mystery of human psychology; on the surface, it seems her husband, Michael, murders her because he believes she is a "changeling" fairy in disguise; investigating this motive.

title: Crimes of the Century: A Selective History of Infamy
description:
S01 E03 — The Sarajevo Conspiracy of 1914
The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand is one of the most world-shaking events in the 20th century; the motivation behind the murder is rife with conspiracy; diving into a cycle of mystery and violence in early 20th-century Sarajevo.

title: Crimes of the Century: A Selective History of Infamy
description:
S01 E04 — The Plot to Assassinate the Romanovs
Exploring the murder of the Russian Tsar Nicholas and other Romanovs at the hands of the Bolsheviks; for more than a century, the facts of this murder are dissected and debated; time adds few facts but plenty of speculation and myth to this event.

title: Foundations of Western Civilization II: A History of the Modern Western World
description:
S01 E01 — The Importance of the West
An overview of the past 500 years of European history and culture; the system of government; economic structures; science and technology; the literature, art and music.

title: Foundations of Western Civilization II: A History of the Modern Western World
description:
S01 E02 — Geography Is Destiny
How the physical realities of Europe and the Atlantic world shaped its destiny; geography and climate affecting patterns of population, immigration, diplomacy, war, and political and cultural divisions.

title: Foundations of Western Civilization II: A History of the Modern Western World
description:
S01 E03 — Culture Is Destiny
The Great Chain of Being, which assumed an ordered, hierarchical universe in which humans were placed in a particular rank by God; Europe emerging from the Middle Ages; how the concept was challenged and strained by various forces.

title: Foundations of Western Civilization II: A History of the Modern Western World
description:
S01 E04 — Renaissance Humanism - 1350 - 1650
A revived interest in the literary and historical works of classical Greece and Rome; new ideas about the qualifications of a gentleman, the role of women and the expectations of a prince; a resulting emphasis on literacy and education.

title: The Skeptic's Guide to American History
description:
S01 E01 — Religious Toleration in Colonial America?
The key elements of a broadened approach; the study of history with this fast-moving examination of the origins of religious and racial tolerance in America; grasping how the assumptions one has held can differ dramatically from historical reality.

title: The Skeptic's Guide to American History
description:
S01 E02 — Neither American nor Revolutionary?
Understanding history with a look at efforts of the colonists to defend their rights as Englishmen; the ironic role played by European tyrannies in helping establish the nation that would forever change the definition of liberty.

title: The Skeptic's Guide to American History
description:
S01 E03 — The Constitution Did Not Create a Democracy
Gaining a nuanced understanding of what the founders' original intent really is; many of the questions they grapple with divide them for their entire lives; ultimately being bequeathed to their successors and persisting even to this day.

title: The Skeptic's Guide to American History
description:
S01 E04 — Washington - Failures and Real Accomplishments
The hagiography that shapes George Washington's image and undertakes a balanced examination, measuring his military and presidential failings against his numerous successes; some of the successes may be his major contributions to American history.

title: The Skeptic's Guide to American History
description:
S01 E05 — Confusions About Jefferson and Hamilton
Jefferson and Hamilton hold opposing views on policy and constitutional interpretation; their conflict is often thought of in terms of one's contemporary understanding of liberalism and conservatism; it is relevant in very different ways.

title: The History of the Supreme Court
description:
S01 E01 — Personality and Principle
Outlining the Supreme Court's development as an institution; discussing the recurring themes of continuity and change, consensus and conflict, and the societal diversity that creates many of the Court's cases.

title: The History of the Supreme Court
description:
S01 E02 — Shaping the Constitution and the Court
Discussing the factors that led to the drafting of a new Constitution; the debates over the shape of the new government.

title: The History of the Supreme Court
description:
S01 E03 — Ratification and the Bill of Rights
Examining the debates at the Constitutional Convention in 1787 over ratification between the supporting Federalists and the Antifederalists; the addition of the Bill of Rights in 1791; the workings of the Court during its first decade.

title: The History of the Supreme Court
description:
S01 E04 — John Marshall Takes Control
The impact of Marshall's 34-year tenure as Chief Justice is significant and long-lasting, examining his career and influence.

title: The History of the Supreme Court
description:
S01 E05 — Impeachment, Contract, and Federal Power
Examining the impeachment and trial of Justice Samuel Chase; studying several landmark cases that grow out of the rapid growth of the nation in the 19th century.

title: The History of the Supreme Court
description:
S01 E06 — Roger Taney Takes Control
Roger Taney is a fervent advocate of states' rights and slavery; when he becomes Chief Justice after the death of John Marshall, the Court's reading of the Constitution becomes very different.

title: The American Revolution
description:
S01 E01 — The Imperial Crisis, 1763 - 1773
Driven close to financial collapse by the French and Indian War, England turns for help to the colonies that had fought at its side; the new taxes, imposed without representation, outrage people who consider themselves fully English.

title: The American Revolution
description:
S01 E02 — The Ancient Constitution
Britain's understanding of its ancient, although unwritten, style of government places it at odds with that of its colonists; the colonists see in John Locke's theories not a hypothetical thought experiment, but an argument for autonomy.

title: The American Revolution
description:
S01 E03 — \"A Soldier What's Fit for a Soldier\"
What the typical British soldier and officers are like; knowing how the troops are organized and equipped; meeting the forces expected to maintain order in the increasingly rebellious colonies.

title: The American Revolution
description:
S01 E04 — \"How the British Regulars Fired and Fled\"
Tensions escalate and the first Continental Congress convenes; King George III finally heeds a request for reinforcements; nevertheless, the British sorely underestimate American militia and suffer a humiliating defeat at Lexington and Concord.

title: The American Revolution
description:
S01 E05 — Standoff in Boston, 1775
Benedict Arnold helps win a key victory at New York's Fort Ticonderoga; the Second Continental Congress authorizes a new army under George Washington, a soldier aware of the implications of the conflict; the risk of potentially rebellious slaves.

title: A History of England from the Tudors to the Stuarts
description:
S01 E01 — England 1485 - 1714, the First Modern Country
Taking a look at the scope of the series; the significance of English history; why this Early-Modern period is crucial not only to the development of England but to transatlantic civilization itself.

title: A History of England from the Tudors to the Stuarts
description:
S01 E02 — The Land and Its People in 1485 - I
Examining England's so-called "island mentality"; its complicated relationship to both Europe and the Celtic lands of Scotland, Ireland and Wales.

title: A History of England from the Tudors to the Stuarts
description:
S01 E03 — The Land and Its People in 1485 - II
The discussion of the physical world of the English people in 1485 continues; a look at the material and social topography of the English town, manor and village, from its wealthiest residents to its poorest.

title: A History of England from the Tudors to the Stuarts
description:
S01 E04 — The Land and Its People in 1485 - III
Turning to the mental landscape of the English people; focusing on the concept of the "Great Chain of Being"; the unyielding social hierarchy it implies.

title: The Great Tours: England, Scotland and Wales
description:
S01 E01 — Welcome to Britain
Why Great Britain offers so much as a travel destination; thousand-year-old castles and cathedrals; contemporary art museums and scenic hikes; a look at the scope of all Britain has to offer, along with a few unique ideas.

title: The Great Tours: England, Scotland and Wales
description:
S01 E02 — Prehistoric Britain
The beginning of Great Britain's history 5,000 years ago; a mysterious ancient people whose only vestiges are earthworks and stone circles; the massive popularity of Stonehenge; visiting other ancient ruins such as Avebury or Maiden Castle.

title: After the Plague
description:
S01 E01 — Resilience: Rethinking the Black Death
The Black Death's pathology and symptoms, and Chaucer's childhood.

title: After the Plague
description:
S01 E02 — Medieval Globalization and the Black Death
Investigating the public health consequences of globalization in the medieval period.

title: After the Plague
description:
S01 E03 — Death Ships: The Spread of Plague in Europe
The plague's continental path and its varying rates of spread.

title: After the Plague
description:
S01 E04 — Children, Plague, and Grief
Bubonic plague's effect on children and how whole towns cared for orphans.

title: The Late Middle Ages
description:
S01 E01 — Late Middle Ages - Rebirth, Waning, Calamity?
An introduction to the course; its focus on two major questions debated by historians for centuries; whether the 14th and 15th centuries mark the turning point between the medieval and the modern; whether this era is a high or low point for Europe.

title: The Late Middle Ages
description:
S01 E02 — Philip the Fair versus Boniface VIII
Examining the conflict between the king of France and the papacy; the results are a growth of French influence and a weakened papacy; these results shape the religious history of 14th-century Europe.

title: The Late Middle Ages
description:
S01 E03 — Fall of the Templars and the Avignon Papacy
Continued French defiance of papal authority generates a perception of French influence; even though it is exaggerated by influential foreign voices such as Petrarch's, it can diminish the authority of an institution that aspires to universality.

title: The Late Middle Ages
description:
S01 E04 — The Great Papal Schism
Two unusual papal elections produce two popes, one in Rome and the other in Avignon, with each claiming legitimacy; the resulting split, complete with competing lines of popes, divides Christian Europe for nearly two generations.

title: The Industrial Revolution
description:
S01 E01 — Industrialization Is Good for You
Stepping into the story of one of the greatest periods in history; investigating why people should be grateful for the Industrial Revolution, even though there is much to dislike about industrialization.

title: The Industrial Revolution
description:
S01 E02 — Why Was Britain First?
Starting at the beginning in the British Isles; various factors contribute to the birth of the Industrial Revolution, including relative political stability, sophisticated financial institutions, colonial trade and a rising population of workers.

title: The Industrial Revolution
description:
S01 E03 — The Agricultural Revolution
In Britain in the 18th century, new agricultural methods come into being; a look at some of these changes to agriculture, including different uses of the land, the introduction of new crops and the early mechanization of farming.

title: The Industrial Revolution
description:
S01 E04 — Cities and Manufacturing Traditions
Traversing the country to see where industry takes off; starting with a detailed look at the advantages and dangers of life in London; shifting attention to provincial cities and towns, where industrialists face various challenges.

title: War in the Modern World
description:
S01 E01 — Afghanistan and the Nature of Modern War
In the course's inaugural episode, begin to explore the transformation of violent conflicts between major world powers by delving into a particularly recent example: America's 20-year war in Afghanistan.

title: War in the Modern World
description:
S01 E02 — Nightmare Scenarios of Modern War
The factors that explain why wars between great powers look different nowadays, and explore what future conflicts could look like between the United States and two of its major adversaries.

title: War in the Modern World
description:
S01 E03 — The Tools of Modern Warfare
How five contemporary technologies-the Kalashnikov assault rifle, improvised explosive devices, guided missiles, drones, and cyber warfare-redefined the rules of battle and leveled the playing field between world powers and insurgent groups.

title: War in the Modern World
description:
S01 E04 — From World War to Cold War
The series of events that followed World War II from the allied occupation of Germany to the Greek Civil War; how the Soviet Union contended with insurgencies and the beginnings of conflict between the United States and the USSR.

S01 E03 — Fall of the Templars and the Avignon Papacy
Continued French defiance of papal authority generates a perception of French influence; even though it is exaggerated by influential foreign voices such as Petrarch's, it can diminish the authority of an institution that aspires to universality.

title: The Late Middle Ages
description:
S01 E04 — The Great Papal Schism
Two unusual papal elections produce two popes, one in Rome and the other in Avignon, with each claiming legitimacy; the resulting split, complete with competing lines of popes, divides Christian Europe for nearly two generations.

title: The Industrial Revolution
description:
S01 E01 — Industrialization Is Good for You
Stepping into the story of one of the greatest periods in history; investigating why people should be grateful for the Industrial Revolution, even though there is much to dislike about industrialization.

title: The Industrial Revolution
description:
S01 E02 — Why Was Britain First?
Starting at the beginning in the British Isles; various factors contribute to the birth of the Industrial Revolution, including relative political stability, sophisticated financial institutions, colonial trade and a rising population of workers.

title: The Industrial Revolution
description:
S01 E03 — The Agricultural Revolution
In Britain in the 18th century, new agricultural methods come into being; a look at some of these changes to agriculture, including different uses of the land, the introduction of new crops and the early mechanization of farming.

title: The Industrial Revolution
description:
S01 E04 — Cities and Manufacturing Traditions
Traversing the country to see where industry takes off; starting with a detailed look at the advantages and dangers of life in London; shifting attention to provincial cities and towns, where industrialists face various challenges.

title: War in the Modern World
description:
S01 E01 — Afghanistan and the Nature of Modern War
In the course's inaugural episode, begin to explore the transformation of violent conflicts between major world powers by delving into a particularly recent example: America's 20-year war in Afghanistan.

title: War in the Modern World
description:
S01 E02 — Nightmare Scenarios of Modern War
The factors that explain why wars between great powers look different nowadays, and explore what future conflicts could look like between the United States and two of its major adversaries.

title: War in the Modern World
description:
S01 E03 — The Tools of Modern Warfare
How five contemporary technologies-the Kalashnikov assault rifle, improvised explosive devices, guided missiles, drones, and cyber warfare-redefined the rules of battle and leveled the playing field between world powers and insurgent groups.

title: War in the Modern World
description:
S01 E04 — From World War to Cold War
The series of events that followed World War II from the allied occupation of Germany to the Greek Civil War; how the Soviet Union contended with insurgencies and the beginnings of conflict between the United States and the USSR.

title: After the Plague
description:
S01 E01 — Resilience: Rethinking the Black Death
The Black Death's pathology and symptoms, and Chaucer's childhood.

title: After the Plague
description:
S01 E02 — Medieval Globalization and the Black Death
Investigating the public health consequences of globalization in the medieval period.

title: After the Plague
description:
S01 E03 — Death Ships: The Spread of Plague in Europe
The plague's continental path and its varying rates of spread.

title: After the Plague
description:
S01 E04 — Children, Plague, and Grief
Bubonic plague's effect on children and how whole towns cared for orphans.

title: The Late Middle Ages
description:
S01 E01 — Late Middle Ages - Rebirth, Waning, Calamity?
An introduction to the course; its focus on two major questions debated by historians for centuries; whether the 14th and 15th centuries mark the turning point between the medieval and the modern; whether this era is a high or low point for Europe.

title: The Late Middle Ages
description:
S01 E02 — Philip the Fair versus Boniface VIII
Examining the conflict between the king of France and the papacy; the results are a growth of French influence and a weakened papacy; these results shape the religious history of 14th-century Europe.

title: Communism in Decline: From Sputnik to Gorbachev

Learn why Sputnik's launch marked communism's peak prestige, as historians explain its global impact and significance.

Examine USSR's complex ties with Cuba and growing rivalry with China: Cold War relationships and communist power dynamics explored.

title: Sex in the Middle Ages
description:

Professor McNabb and the expert panel consider medieval ideas about procreation and examine how everyday people thought about their own bodies.

description:
S01 E03 — Breaking the Rules of Medieval Sex Taboos

title: Sex in the Middle Ages
